Unencoded Elements

Source: R/io-legacy.R
io-legacy.Rd

Reads Elements written without encoding-type and encoding-version attributes (read_basic), as old anndata releases did. Each one raises anndata_old_format_warning, as Python's OldFormatWarning. A group is read as a dict and a dataset as an array or scalar, and a group with the h5sparse attributes h5sparse_format and h5sparse_shape is read as a CSR or CSC matrix. A compound dataset with array-valued fields (old obsm and varm) is read as a list of matrices, one per field. The member types of a compound dataset come from the compiled helper (ADR 0008), so numeric fields keep their on-disk dtype records (such as float32). Writing always uses the current encodings.

Usage

read_unencoded_elem(elem, path, store, call)

Arguments

elem

An open group or dataset handle.

path

Path of the Element.

store

The store elem was opened from.

call

The call reported by conditions.

Details

Legacy files also read with read_h5ad(backed = ) (an unencoded dense X or h5sparse X stays on disk) and rewrite to the current encodings. read_lazy() follows Python and only reads the current encodings, so it raises for the legacy layouts, and it does not move uns$neighbors matrices to obsp.
